questions.q: Why does a flow that needs to act on individual values prefer JSON output over free text from a prompt?
options: JSON output runs faster on every request
Free text packs multiple answers into one paragraph, requiring extra steps to split them apart; JSON returns each answer as its own key, usable immediately
Text output is no longer supported by AI Builder
JSON output requires no prompt instructions at all
questions.explain: A text response bundles multiple answers together, forcing extra parsing. JSON output gives each value its own key, ready as individual dynamic content.

questions.q: Where do you switch a prompt's output from Text to JSON?
options: In the flow designer's trigger settings
A toggle in the top-right corner of the prompt builder's editor
In the Power Automate admin center
It switches automatically based on the input type
questions.explain: The output type selector, which lets you choose Text or JSON, sits in the top-right corner of the prompt editor in prompt builder.

questions.q: What is the key difference between auto-detected and custom JSON format?
options: Auto-detected is inferred fresh each time you test the prompt; custom locks the format to an example you provide, so it won't silently change later
Custom format requires no example at all
Auto-detected format can never be changed once set
There is no functional difference
questions.explain: Auto-detected refreshes the format on every test run based on what the model returned. Custom format locks to your own example and stays fixed even as you keep editing the prompt's instructions.

questions.q: For a production flow like the one you'll build in Lesson 13, which JSON format should you prefer, and why?
options: Auto-detected, because it requires less setup
Custom, because it keeps the key names stable so downstream actions don't break if the model's output shifts
Neither — JSON output should never be used in production
It doesn't matter; both behave identically in production
questions.explain: Custom format locks in exact key names a flow downstream can depend on, whereas auto-detected format can shift based on what the model happens to return during testing.

questions.q: What happens if a JSON-output prompt's response doesn't come back as valid JSON when the flow runs?
options: The flow silently continues with blank values
The action surfaces an error rather than silently returning garbage
Power Automate automatically rewrites the prompt's instructions
The flow converts it to plain text instead
questions.explain: An invalid JSON response causes the action to surface an error. A common cause is the model wrapping its answer in markdown code fences, often fixed by an explicit instruction not to include markdown.
